To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

single-fraction palliation radiotherapy (8 Gy) yields comparable outcomes as long-course (≥10 fractions), in patients with breast cancer bone metastases, and that patients with favorable baseline characteristics are more likely to receive the long-course PRT, which might be due to a lack of knowledge about single-fraction PRR in this rural area with long travel distance.

the majority of Norwegian female patients with bone metastasis from breast cancer receive guideline-conform PRT with long courses (60%) or single fraction of 4 Gy (20%), while 20% are treated with single fraction of 6 or 8 Gy.

the use of single-fraction palliation radiotherapy (Prt) for bone metastasis from breast cancer is safe and effective, and that patients with favorable baseline characteristics are more likely to receive longer fractionation schedules.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the implementation of single-fraction PBT for bone metastases in a rural part, 2) the association between baseline characteristics and fractionation regimen, 3) the association between clinical factors and survival in patients with bone-only disease from breast cancer.
the clinical benefit of PRT for bone metastases from primary breast cancer and its association with different fractionation regims.
the implementation of evidence-based medicine in the rural part of Norway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
single-fraction 8-Gy PRT is as effective as long-course PRT, and that the latter should be reserved for selected patients.
single-fraction 8 Gy PRT is as effective and as safe as long-course PRT for palliation of bone metastases in breast cancer patients.
single-fraction 8 Gy PRT is an effective and safe alternative to long-course PRT, which should be offered to patients with breast cancer and bone metastases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with bone metastatic breast cancer can be treated with single fraction PRT with a low rate of reirradiation, even with poor PS.
single-fraction radiotherapy is a convenient and safe treatment option that should be offered to more patients with bone metastasis from breast cancer.
single fraction PRT is a feasible and effective treatment option in patients with bone-metastatic breast cancer, especially in those with poor PS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
single-fraction 8 Gy PRT is a viable alternative to long-course treatment in the management of bone metastasis from breast cancer.
single-fraction radiotherapy should be considered for patients with bone metastasis from breast cancer, regardless of PS.
patients with breast cancer bone metastases should be treated with single-fraction P RT, unless they have a poor prognosis.
